description: Azure Table and Blob storage-aware state manager support for Egil.Orleans.Messaging.
releaseNotes:
BREAKING CHANGES:
- capture producer trace context when adding to the outbox
  Outbox messages now carry the W3C traceparent of the activity that was current
  when the message was added, so work done by the receiving grain can be
  correlated with the request that produced the message.
  Capture happens at append time rather than at delivery time. The processor
  drains on a grain timer, on a reminder, or on whichever request happens to
  trigger the drain, so by delivery the producing activity has usually ended. A
  drain also flushes every pending message in one run with groups dispatched
  concurrently, so reading the ambient activity at delivery would attribute a
  message added by one request to an unrelated one — a wrong link that is
  indistinguishable from a right one when reading a trace.
  At delivery the processor starts one orleans.outbox.post producer span per
  message, linked to the captured context, and invokes the postman inside it.
  Postmen that propagate Activity.Current — Orleans grain calls, and stream
  adapters such as EnrichedEventHubAdapter that stamp a traceparent onto the
  queued message — therefore carry the right trace to the receiver without
  changes of their own.
  The producing context is attached as a link rather than as a parent because a
  message can be delivered hours after the producing request ended, and parenting
  into a finished trace produces orphaned spans and traces that stretch across
  the whole delay.
  tracestate is not captured: it is vendor data of up to 512 bytes, and the
  outbox is rewritten inside the grain state record on every WriteStateAsync for
  as long as a message stays pending. The traceparent is stored regardless of the
  sampled flag, so the trace id remains usable as the join key between logs and
  traces even when the producing span was never exported.
  TraceParent, defaulting to null, and OutboxSequenceToken gains a TraceParent
  property with TryGetTraceParent(out string?). OutboxMessageId equality now
  includes TraceParent, so an id rebuilt by hand from a sequence number,
  timestamp, and epoch no longer matches the stored id of a message added under
  an active Activity; pass the id from outbox.Envelopes[i].Id to Remove and
  RemoveRange instead. The property is nullable and omitted from JSON when
  absent, so snapshots written before this change load unchanged and no migration
  or reset is required.
Bug Fixes:
- make the concurrent dispatch test actually dispatch concurrently
  The test registered a postman per item to force two dispatch groups, but the
  postman blocked on Barrier.SignalAndWait synchronously. The dispatcher starts
  groups in a loop and only reaches the second once the first awaits, so the
  first group waited for a group that was never started. SignalAndWait returns
  false on timeout rather than throwing, so after 30 seconds per item the test
  continued and passed while asserting nothing about concurrency — and the core
  test project took a minute instead of two seconds.
  The postman now yields before rendezvousing, and the rendezvous awaits a
  TaskCompletionSource with WaitAsync so a regression that serialises the groups
  fails the test instead of passing slowly. The span recorder uses a
  ConcurrentBag, because genuinely concurrent groups stop their spans on
  different continuations and can invoke ActivityStopped in parallel.
  Also documents that the added optional constructor parameters are binary
  breaking and that OutboxMessageId's generated Deconstruct is now four-valued.
- keep trace context out of outbox message identity
  OutboxMessageId and OutboxSequenceToken are records, so adding TraceParent
  silently pulled it into equality and hash code. That broke two documented
  invariants: an id rebuilt from its sequence number, timestamp, and epoch no
  longer matched the stored id of a message added under an active Activity, and
  MessageTracker.LatestOutbox stopped returning a token equal to the one it
  accepted, because the tracker stores no traceparent.
  Exclude TraceParent from equality on both types. The alternative — persisting
  the traceparent in the tracker entry — would hold stale trace context in the
  receiver's durable state, per sender, for a message it had already processed.
  Failed deliveries now also mark the dispatch span with an error status and
  exception tags, matching StreamManager, so a delivery that threw no longer
  exports as Unset and reads as a success in a trace viewer.
title: Orleans Messaging Azure Storage State Manager
